claims.text: The initial material is a near-equiatomic AlCoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy.
The proposed intervention increases the relative Al content of the AlCoCrFeNi-based alloy.
The proposed intervention adds a modest, controlled amount of Ti to the alloy.
Increasing Al and adding Ti promotes in situ spinel-oxide formation during elevated-temperature friction.
The resulting spinel oxide is coherent and adherent to the alloy surface during wear.
The spinel oxide acts as a self-healing layer.
The spinel oxide provides a physical barrier that impedes mechanical wear.
The spinel oxide provides a physical barrier that impedes corrosive attack.
The protective layer reduces diffusion and oxidation kinetics at the alloy surface.
The modified alloy will have lower wear depth than conventional alloys or non-optimized AlCoCrFeNi HEAs under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The modified alloy will have lower corrosion rates than conventional alloys or non-optimized AlCoCrFeNi HEAs under identical high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
Reduced wear and corrosion will give the modified alloy enhanced durability.
Unmodified AlCoCrFeNi-based HEAs do not achieve controlled in situ formation of the proposed protective oxide under elevated-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The beneficial effect occurs within a temperature window in which spinel formation is favored.
Performance may diminish outside the favorable temperature or corrosive-condition regime.
The optimal Al and Ti concentration ranges needed to form the desired spinel oxide remain undetermined.
The long-term stability of the oxide layer under cyclic stress is uncertain.
